content.title: About
content.content: Ricotta is a soft Italian cheese made from the whey left over after producing other cheeses (such as mozzarella). It has a delicate creamy flavor, slightly sweet, and a smooth texture. Ricotta is commonly used in desserts, pastas, lasagna, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “ricotta” comes from the Italian “ricotta,” meaning “re‑cooked.”
Traditionally ricotta is made from cow, sheep, or goat whey.
In Italy ricotta is often served with honey and nuts as a dessert.
Ricotta is high in protein but relatively low in fat compared with many other cheeses.
There is a “dry ricotta” variety that is further dehydrated for a firmer consistency.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ricotta provides about 11 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in ricotta helps strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Compared with many hard cheeses, ricotta contains moderate salt levels, which is beneficial for blood pressure control.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ricotta supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Its soft texture and partial fermentation make ricotta gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey proteins may react to ricotta.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Ricotta contains lactose, so those with lactose intolerance should limit intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although less fatty than many cheeses, ricotta is still calorie‑dense and should be consumed in moderation for weight management.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Fresh ricotta spoils quickly; it must be refrigerated and used within its indicated shelf life.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ricotta can be enjoyed on its own, mixed with honey, fruit, or nuts. It is a classic filling for pasta, lasagna, cannelloni, and desserts such as tiramisu and cheesecakes. Add it to smoothies for a creamy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ricotta in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It typically keeps 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if it develops a sour smell or mold.
